requirement:
Configuration names MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and be case-sensitive.
Project-selection keys MUST be canonical absolute project-root paths. Model IDs
MUST be nonempty opaque strings, preserving tags and ARNs. `api_key_env` MUST
name a nonempty environment variable without `=` or NUL.

Authoring MUST validate its fields under {cite}`requirements.configuration.loading`.
The `options` map MUST accept backend-defined inference settings rather than a
closed Habeas list; the adapter MUST pass them through Rig's provider parameter
mechanism and report rejection by Rig or the provider. These options MUST NOT
replace the selected model, the assessment prompt, or tool definitions.
rationale:
## Judgment

The implementation and referenced tests satisfy `requirements.authoring.configuration_storage`. No unacknowledged gap was found.

## Obligations and coverage

- **Configuration names match the stated pattern.** `src/config.rs#fn[validate_name]` checks the first byte for ASCII alphanumeric membership and every byte for ASCII alphanumeric, underscore, or hyphen membership. It is reached through `src/config.rs#impl[UserAuthoringConfig]/fn[validate]` from the marked `UserConfig::parse` root. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[storage_rules_reject_each_invalid_field_with_its_setting]` tests empty names, invalid initial characters, punctuation, whitespace, non-ASCII names, and accepted mixed-character names.
- **Names are case-sensitive.** The string-keyed `BTreeMap` in `src/config.rs#struct[UserAuthoringConfig]` preserves case, and `src/config.rs#fn[resolve_authoring_with_workspace_from]` performs exact lookups. The storage-rules test asserts that `Local` and `local` coexist; `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs]` asserts that selecting `DEFAULT` does not select `default`.
- **Project-selection keys are absolute and canonical.** `src/config.rs#impl[UserAuthoringConfig]/fn[validate]` rejects relative paths, noncanonical component spelling, and existing paths whose canonical spelling differs. The storage-rules test covers relative paths, parent and current-directory components, trailing separators, symlinks on Unix, and accepted canonical paths. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[user_and_workspace_authoring_tables_round_trip_every_map]` additionally checks preservation of a canonical project key.
- **Model IDs are nonempty, opaque strings that preserve tags and ARNs.** `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[validate]` rejects empty effective IDs without interpreting their syntax; `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[model_ref]` preserves their contents. The storage-rules test covers empty IDs and exact tagged identifiers. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[user_and_workspace_authoring_tables_round_trip_every_map]` asserts exact Bedrock ARN and model-ID preservation, while `tests/configuration.rs#fn[backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults]` covers tagged Ollama IDs and configuration round trips.
- **`api_key_env` is nonempty and contains neither `=` nor NUL.** `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[validate]` checks each property. The storage-rules test separately rejects all three invalid forms and accepts a valid name.
- **Authoring validates its fields under `requirements.configuration.loading`.** The marked `src/config.rs#impl[UserConfig]/fn[parse]` decodes and validates; the marked `resolve_authoring_from` reaches validation of both supplied user and workspace configurations through `src/config.rs#fn[resolve_authoring_with_workspace_from]`. Workspace validation applies the same field checks. The storage-rules test asserts file and setting identification for invalid user and workspace fields. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[invalid_schema_and_feature_values_report_the_configuration_path]` and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[authoring_concurrency_defaults_overrides_and_invalid_values]` provide additional invalid-field coverage. This assesses application of the cited loading requirement to authoring, not that requirement independently.
- **Options accept backend-defined inference settings.** Validation iterates arbitrary option keys rather than a closed inference-setting list. `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[options_json]` serializes that map. The round-trip tests exercise arbitrary nested provider settings; the referenced Ollama, Bedrock, and OpenAI CLI tests assert their delivery in provider requests.
- **The adapter passes options through Rig's provider parameter mechanism.** `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[RigProvider/CompletionProvider]/fn[complete]` sets `additional_params`; its reachable `apply_bedrock_options` maps native Converse fields onto Rig request fields and leaves additional provider fields in the map. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]`, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]`, and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` assert the respective wire outcomes.
- **Rig rejection and provider rejection are reported.** `complete` propagates native-option validation failures and wraps model-call failures through `src/authoring/providers.rs#fn[provider_failure]`. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[provider_rejection_of_inference_options_is_reported]` asserts both a provider rejection diagnostic and a pre-request Bedrock option-type diagnostic. The referenced Bedrock unit test covers additional invalid native option types.
- **Options cannot replace the selected model, assessment prompt, or tool definitions.** `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[validate]` rejects the reserved model, prompt/history, and tool keys. The storage-rules test exercises the three categories; `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_configuration_preserves_model_and_resolves_credentials]` additionally rejects OpenAI `input` and `instructions`. The CLI request tests assert selected models, assessment prompt content, and tool definitions alongside passed-through options.

The finite-value restriction is specified by `requirements.authoring.configuration_structure`; OpenAI option defaults are specified by `requirements.authoring.openai_defaults`; credential checks are specified by `requirements.authoring.credentials`; and checkpoint handling is specified by `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`. These are not unspecified extra behaviors.

text: :::{req} configuration_storage
Configuration names MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and be case-sensitive.
Project-selection keys MUST be canonical absolute project-root paths. Model IDs
MUST be nonempty opaque strings, preserving tags and ARNs. `api_key_env` MUST
name a nonempty environment variable without `=` or NUL.
Authoring MUST validate its fields under {cite}`requirements.configuration.loading`.
The `options` map MUST accept backend-defined inference settings rather than a
closed Habeas list; the adapter MUST pass them through Rig's provider parameter
mechanism and report rejection by Rig or the provider. These options MUST NOT
replace the selected model, the assessment prompt, or tool definitions.
:::{req} loading
An operation MUST load user configuration only when its requirements call for
user settings. A missing user file MUST represent absent user configuration;
whether the operation can proceed MUST be defined by the feature. Loading MUST
NOT create a file, repair malformed input, or supply an undocumented selection.
When loading configuration, Habeas MUST report unreadable files, invalid TOML,
unsupported user-file versions, unknown common keys, and invalid common field
types. It MUST validate the feature sections used by that operation and report
invalid feature settings with the file and setting identified. Unknown keys in
an explicitly documented provider-owned options map MUST follow that feature's
validation rules.
An operation MUST NOT require or semantically validate configuration for a
feature it does not use. This isolation MUST NOT suppress TOML syntax errors in
a shared file that the operation otherwise needs to parse. In particular,
ordinary validation still requires a parseable `book.toml` while remaining
independent of authoring settings and the user configuration file. It MUST apply
the selected workspace's evidence path policy without loading its model clients
or credentials.
:::{req} configuration_structure
Habeas MUST define its authoring configuration using these data structures:
```text
UserAuthoringConfig {
default: Optional<ConfigName>,
configs: Map<ConfigName, AuthoringConfig>,
projects: Map<CanonicalProjectRoot, ProjectSelection>,
WorkspaceAuthoringConfig {
default: Optional<ConfigName>,
configs: Map<ConfigName, AuthoringConfig>,  // omitted means empty
ProjectSelection {
config: ConfigName,
AuthoringConfig {
backend: BackendConfig,                   // tagged union, flattened in TOML
concurrency: Optional<PositiveInteger>,   // simultaneous assessments
policy: Optional<AssessmentPolicy>,       // default: Confirm
AssessmentPolicy = Confirm | Once             // TOML: "confirm" or "once"
BackendConfig = Bedrock(BedrockConfig) | Ollama(OllamaConfig) | Openai(OpenAiConfig)
BedrockConfig {
model: ModelId,                           // model ID or inference-profile ID/ARN
aws_profile: Optional<String>,
region: Optional<String>,
credentials: Optional<BedrockCredentials>,
options: Map<String, OptionValue>,
BedrockCredentials {
access_key_id: SecretString,
secret_access_key: SecretString,
session_token: Optional<SecretString>,
OllamaConfig {
model: ModelId,                           // exact identifier, including tag
endpoint: Optional<String>,               // default: http://localhost:11434
api_key_env: Optional<EnvironmentVariableName>,
api_key: Optional<SecretString>,
options: Map<String, OptionValue>,
OpenAiConfig {
model: Optional<ModelId>,                 // default: gpt-6.1-sol
endpoint: Optional<String>,               // default: https://api.openai.com/v1
api_key_env: Optional<EnvironmentVariableName>, // default: OPENAI_API_KEY
api_key: Optional<SecretString>,
options: Map<String, OptionValue>,
OptionValue = String | Boolean | Integer | FiniteFloat
| Array<OptionValue> | Map<String, OptionValue>
SecretString = String                         // serialized normally; redacted in Debug
ModelRef {
backend: BackendKind,                     // Bedrock, Ollama, or Openai
model: ModelId,
`ModelRef` MUST be derived from the selected backend configuration and MUST
preserve the exact model identifier. It MUST identify the model without replacing
connection settings such as AWS profile, region, or Ollama endpoint.
:::{req} rig_configuration_mapping
Habeas MUST resolve its saved configuration before constructing Rig provider
clients and completion models. The Habeas data structures MUST remain the saved
format. Rig model references MAY be reused internally without discarding the
connection settings they do not represent.
The Bedrock adapter MUST pass the chosen AWS profile and region through AWS SDK
configuration, or use explicitly configured credentials. The Ollama adapter MUST use the chosen server, exact model ID,
and optional authentication; the server MAY be local or remote. The OpenAI adapter MUST use the Responses API, selected endpoint, exact model
ID, and resolved API key. All adapters
MUST supply the same tools and initial prompt.
:::{req} openai_defaults
An OpenAI configuration MAY omit `model`; the effective model MUST then be
`gpt-6.1-sol`. When `options.reasoning.effort` is omitted, the request MUST use
`low` effort, preserving other reasoning options. When `options.max_output_tokens`
is omitted, the request MUST use an output-token limit of 16,384. These option
defaults MUST apply even when the model is overridden. An explicit model,
reasoning effort, or output-token limit MUST override its corresponding default.
Defaults MUST NOT be written into omitted configuration fields on serialization.
An explicitly empty model MUST still be rejected.
:::{req} cache_checkpoints
When the backend and model support prompt caching, every provider request MUST
place one cache checkpoint after the system prompt of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and another at the end of its last
message, so each request reuses the tool definitions and system prompt that
earlier assessments of its kind sent, and the conversation its own earlier
requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT change the content of a request.
:::{req} credentials
Bedrock configurations MAY supply `credentials` containing nonempty
`access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, and optional nonempty `session_token`.
Ollama and OpenAI configurations MAY supply a nonempty `api_key`. Habeas MUST reject a
Bedrock record combining explicit credentials with `aws_profile`, and an Ollama or OpenAI
record combining `api_key` with `api_key_env`.
Explicit credentials MUST be passed directly to the selected provider without
changing process environment variables or writing credential files. Saved
explicit values MUST round-trip; credentials resolved from profiles or the
environment MUST NOT be serialized back. Debug output, configuration diagnostics,
usage records, and initial prompts MUST NOT include credential values. TOML
diagnostics MUST NOT echo credential-containing source lines. A configuration
file containing explicit credentials MAY be read as source; its credential
values MUST be redacted under {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`.
Validation MUST report a workspace `habeas.toml` present in the Git index that
contains explicit credentials, naming the file and the credential fields and
recommending credential-source references, because committed credentials leak.
Documentation MUST discourage literal credentials in workspace files and
recommend AWS profiles or environment-variable references. Examples MUST use
placeholders and explain that workspace files may be committed or read as source
when explicitly allowed.
